subject: Dedicated capacity recap — Acme Health discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap — Acme Health discovery follow-up

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary of pain / goals
- Production latency spikes at peak (medication reconciliation workflows) — p95 currently ~850ms, p99 > 1.5s.
- Data isolation & PHI requirements: must be VPC-isolated with customer-managed KMS.
- Predictable throughput for nightly batch processing (large batch windows) and sub-200ms interactive SLOs for UI paths.

Redwood Dedicated recommendation (high-level)
- Baseline reserved capacity: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) to cover predictable throughput.
- Burst policy: allow up to 16 GPUs for scheduled batch windows and spikes.
- Isolation: VPC peering + private control plane; optional on-prem agent for full air-gap if needed.
- SLA targets: 99.9% uptime for serving endpoints; p95 latency goal <300ms on typical short prompts (we’ll validate on your prompts).

Operational notes / assumptions
- We’ll enable prefix/KV caching for user sessions to improve interactive latency.
- Quantization profile: FP16 for quality-critical endpoints; INT8 QC for lower-cost batch paths where acceptable.
- Assumed average request size ~150 tokens and batch-friendly burst patterns at 2AM local time. Please flag if those numbers are off.

Attachments: I’ve attached a capacity plan draft (acme_health_capacity_plan_v1.xlsx) and our Dedicated terms (redwood-dedicated-terms.pdf).

Next steps
1) Alex — confirm baseline expected RPS during peak interactive hours and nightly batch concurrency.
2) We’ll run a small benchmark using a representative prompt set (we can mirror via S3 / sample prompts).
3) If numbers look good, we’ll create a preliminary SOW + capacity config for legal/procurement.

Would you be available for a 30-min follow-up on Monday to lock the RPS numbers?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

---
Attachments: acme_health_capacity_plan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-dedicated-terms.pdf (PDF)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap — Acme Health discovery follow-up

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and for sending the attachments. Confirming a few items from our side and adding some more detail:

Confirmations / clarifications
- Peak interactive RPS: roughly 45 RPS across our UI cluster during business hours (08:00–20:00 PT). Spikes to ~90 RPS for short bursts (30–90s).
- Nightly batch: concurrency of around 120 parallel model jobs between 02:00–04:00; each job ~1–2k tokens.
- Security: we require customer-managed KMS and audit logs delivered to our SIEM; SOC 2 attestation is also required for vendor onboarding.

Questions
1) For the proposed 8x baseline, do you expect sustained p95 <300ms for 45 RPS with our request size, or will we need bigger baseline for headroom?
2) Can you confirm cost delta for enabling burst to 16 GPUs vs. on-demand burst?

We’re happy to run the benchmark with sample prompts. I’ve attached a small CSV with representative prompt lengths and categories (see attached). If you can run the validation benchmark early next week, we’ll prioritize procurement internally.

Thanks — available for Monday 11:00 AM PT for the follow-up.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Platform Lead, Acme Health
alex.johnson@acmehealth.com | (617) 555-1222

---
Attachments: acme_prompt_samples.csv (CSV)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 17:28:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity recap — Acme Health discovery follow-up

Marissa — looping back after Alex’s note. Quick internal plan:

- Book benchmark slot for Monday 08:00–10:00 PT (run across baseline 8 GPUs and burst to 16). I’ll request access to their sample CSV and S3 location.
- Validate p95/p99 on their 150-token UI prompts and 1–2k token batch jobs.
- Prepare three PO-ready configs: (1) baseline 8 GPU reserved w/ burst to 16, (2) baseline 12 GPUs reserved, (3) baseline 8 GPUs + on-demand burst pricing estimate. Include estimated monthly costs and expected p95 latency for each.
- Schedule follow-up call with Alex Mon 11:00 AM PT (confirmed).

I’ll own the cost estimates and the SOW draft. Can you run the initial benchmark and capture p95/p99 and token cost breakdown? Also capture any prompts that need model-variant fallbacks during burst.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
